roleDifferences: Local sequence allocation versus remote HLC observation
Materialized Yjs update, revision and provenance times: authored clock locally, receive wall clock remotely; provenance source system/remote
exemptions: Seed yjs.update payloads differ by design: native seeds one empty paragraph with a stable block id and caches it; the renderer seeds the category "{}" template as an empty fragment and caches "{}". Seeds are compared by decoded Yjs structure; every other byte of the original and every renderer authority row match.

element/element_category content_json compares as parsed JSON (native key-sorted, reducer ProseMirror key order). A restore re-projects the reducer cache from authoritative Yjs while native, like the renderer restore, preserves the existing cache; each role is verified.
The renderer repository softDelete/restore stamps its own row with the wall clock; native and the originals use the authored clock.
An alias-only update carries no element field: the authoring side stamps element.updated_at (native and the renderer repository alike) while a receiving reducer keeps the previous value.
carriedOwnerState: A retired element body owner re-stamps its checkpoint (yjs_snapshots.updated_at, identical bytes) while trashing; for documents no mutation of the original targets, that row is carried from the native after-database, and every other owner row must be unchanged.
reducerDefects: TS remote alias projection (materializeSet) collects present members of every incarnation: after a restore the reducer writes element.aliases_json with the trashed incarnation's aliases repeated, where native and the renderer local path write the live incarnation only. Pinned to both restores; OR-set tags and every other column match.
renderer.scope: Native element category and element create/update/trash/restore originals match the renderer use cases authored on the same prior state (byte-identical except seed Yjs), production reducer SQLite effects, the production element/category repositories, alias OR-set projection and authoritative body Yjs. No native remote receive, provider transport or UI acceptance.

boundaries.source: Real native element category and element create, update, trash and restore commands over synthetic file-backed workspaces.
agreedGroups: Create a category and a default-named element, rename it with NFKC aliases, clear its group and recolour the category; the body owner edits, undoes and cold-reopens independently of chapters.
Trash retires the open body owner and hides the element; restore reauthors the next incarnation with every alias and the complete body state, which reopens editable without prose undo history.

A receipt failure before each command leaves state intact and each retry writes exactly one canonical original; invalid categories, colours, name conflicts, lifecycle and unknown fields are refused without writes.
boundaries.rendererParity: The renderer use cases (useElementCategory, useBookElement, normalized-kv-alias-authority, sync-lifecycle-restore) run through the production authored runner on each prior native database and author byte-identical originals except seed Yjs, with identical journal, lifecycle, field-clock, OR-set, order and KV rows and the same element/category row. The production decoder, reducer transaction and repositories consume the actual native originals; twenty tables match under the listed roles, rows equal the native command result and aliases_json equals the live alias displays in member order.

limitations: Native local element library commands; the TypeScript remote reducer is a compatibility oracle, not a native remote receive or provider transport claim.
Exported steps only add aliases; alias removal and display replacement (set.remove with observedAddTags) are core-test evidence and are checked here only if an exported step emits them.
Category templates, element facts, portraits, relations, category trash/restore and permanent deletion are refused natively and not covered.
Element body prose edits, undo/redo and reopen are native bridge-test evidence; body edits are not exported originals here.
Synthetic in-process receipt failure and cold reopen; no SIGKILL, power loss, UI, physical device, cloud account or release acceptance.
